column3: Pure substances:  consists of a single type of particle. Substance is pure, single form of matter.

column5: Elements: Pure substance that contains only one type of atoms. e.g. Copper, Iron.

column8: Solid Elements: Solid at Room temperature. e.g. Copper, Gold.
Liquid Elements: Liquid at Room temperature. e.g. Bromine, Mercury.
Gaseous Elements: Gas at Room temperature. e.g. Oxygen, Nitrogen etc.
Metals: It is an element which is ductile, Malleable and conducts electricity. e.g. Iron, Gold, Copper etc.
Non-Metals: Substances which is neither ductile nor malleable or conducts electricity. e.g. Oxygen, Diamond, Potassium .
Metalloids: Elements which has properties in between metal and non-metal. e.g. Silicon, Boron etc.

column5: Compounds: Pure substance which is composed of 2 or more elements, that have been combined chemically in a fixed ratio by mass. e.g. Methane, Water, CO2

column3: Mixture: It is made-up of 2 or more different chemical substances which are not combined chemically. e.g. lemonade, Cold-drink, Milk Shake.

column8: Size more than 1 nm, can be seen by naked eyes.
Further classified in Colloidal solution and Suspension.

column5: Homogeneous Mixture: It is called true solution.

column6: Solution = Solvent + Solute. e.g. Salt Solution = Water + Salt

column10: Shave Cream, Cold drink (CO2 in Water)
Water in sugar or salt, Jelly

column7: Particles of a solution are smaller than 1 nm (10^-9 m) in diameter so they cannot be seen by naked eyes.
Because of very small particle size they don't scatter light passing through the solution (no Tindal effect)
Defined as the amount of solution present in given amount (mass or volume) of solution.
Concentration of solution = (Amount of solute)/(Amount of Solvent)
Percentage method is most common method of expressing concentration of solution

column8: Mass-Mass percentage = (Mass of Solute(gm))/(Mass of Solvent(gm))×100
Mass-Volume percentage = (Mass of Solute(gm))/(Volume of Solvent(ml))×100
Volume-Volume percentage = (Volume of Solute(ml))/(Volume of Solvent(ml))×100

column5: Suspension: Heterogeneous mixture in which particles do not dissolve, but remain suspended throughout bulk of the medium. Particles visible to naked eye (show Tindal Effect). e.g Mixture of chalk power and water, Mixture of wheat flour and water.

column7: Particles of suspension scatter a wave of light passing through it and make its path visible.

column5: Colloidal solution: These are Heterogeneous Mixture, that appear homogeneous. To avoid confusion with true solution the term "Sol" is used in place of solution. E.g. milk, blood etc.

column7: Colloids are big enough to scatter beam of light passing through to make path visible.
They do not settle down when left undisturbed, that is, a colloid is quiet stable.

column2: Physical Changes: Changes in Physical Properties (no change in chemical properties) is called Physical Change.
Chemical Changes: Change in Chemical Properties. It is also called Chemical reaction. It gives completely new substances.
Antoine Laurent Lavoisier: Established experimentally useful definition of element.

column3: He defined element as basic form of matter that cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical reaction.
